title: Building the streaming my speech model did not ship
subtitle: The open-weight voice model I chose had no streaming hook, so I ported its token loop, decoded its audio in chunks and pinned its diffusion noise so the joins are seamless

stats.label: tokens before the first chunk is released
voices registered, each persona with its own

lede: The voice model was chosen in a bake-off on the criteria that matter in a conversation: time to first audio, real-time factor, memory, licence, voice cloning and streaming. The winner carried a permissive licence. One law came out of the bake-off and stands over every voice on the site: never clone a real human voice without documented consent. The winner had one problem. Its released package produced audio in a batch: about 1.6 seconds to the first sound regardless of how short the sentence was. That is a fixed tax on every reply, and the package exposed no way to stream.
quote: A small patch over the sampler is the difference between streaming that works and streaming that crackles.
evidence: Speech synthesis engineering: streaming built for an open-weight voice model that had none, cutting time to first audio to about 0.3 s from about 1.6.
Model evaluation and selection: 8 synthesisers compared on time to first audio, real-time factor, memory, licence, voice cloning and streaming.
Diffusion sampling control: noise pinned across chunk overlaps so every join renders identically and streams without clicks, first chunk after 12 tokens.
Responsible voice AI: 56 registered voices under a rule never to clone a real human voice without documented consent.
author: Corey James
